title: Tagliatelle Bolognese
subtitle: The authentic slow-cooked Bolognese ragu
excerpt: A slow-cooked meat ragu from Bologna: beef and pork mince cooked for 2 to 3 hours with wine, milk, and a soffritto of onion, celery, and carrot. Served with fresh tagliatelle and Parmesan.

recipe.sourceNotes: The ragu bolognese was officially registered with the Bologna Chamber of Commerce in 1982 to establish the authentic recipe. The original contains no garlic, no tinned tomatoes (only tomato paste), and no dried herbs: just the soffritto, two types of meat, wine, and milk. The milk tenderises the meat and rounds the acidity of the wine. The sauce must cook for at least 2 hours; 3 is better. The British spaghetti bolognese is a different dish: the authentic pairing is fresh tagliatelle.

content.text: The minimum cooking time is 2 hours; 3 hours gives a better result. The sauce should barely simmer throughout, with just an occasional bubble. Add a splash of water or beef stock if it threatens to dry out. The meat should be very finely crumbled rather than left in clumps: break it down with a wooden spoon as it cooks.

Melt the butter in a heavy-based saucepan over medium-low heat. Fry the pancetta for 3 minutes. Add the onion, celery, and carrot. Cook slowly for 10 minutes until very soft and just beginning to colour.

Increase the heat to medium-high. Add the beef and pork mince. Break up with a wooden spoon and cook until the meat has lost its pink colour and any liquid has evaporated. Add the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute.

Add the wine. Stir until absorbed. Add the milk. Stir until absorbed. Add the beef stock. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a bare simmer. Cook uncovered over very low heat for 2 to 3 hours, stirring every 20 minutes, until the sauce is thick and rich.
Cook the tagliatelle according to packet instructions. Reserve 200 ml pasta water. Drain. Add to the ragu with a splash of pasta water. Toss to combine. Serve with Parmesan.
